newsitem.title: USA: U.S. education jobs post sharp Sept drop-Labor.
newsitem.headline: U.S. education jobs post sharp Sept drop-Labor.

text.p: The number of local teaching jobs dropped sharply in September because of seasonal adjustment factors, contributing to a decline in overall government payrolls, the U.S. Labor Department said.
The September employment data released earlier on Friday showed an 81,000-job drop in government employment. That drop included a decline of 67,000 local education jobs, the department said.
The service-producing sector, which includes both the government and the education categories, posted a weak performance as a result, with growth of a mere 10,000 jobs.

The department pegged those declines to the impact of changes in school year schedules on its method of adjusting data for seasonal factors. In August, the number of local teaching jobs rose by 85,000.

"Due to changes in school schedules, there were larger returns to payrolls prior to September this year than were expected by our seasonal factors," said Katharine Abraham, commissioner of the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics.
"This accounts for the large increases, on a seasonally adjusted basis, in local education employment over the summer and for this month's sharp decline," she said in a statement.
